title: Integration tests for match result recording and leaderboard
name: Match result integration tests

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this integration test is set up to verify the service against its database? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does the test class use a PostgreSQL Testcontainer instead of an in-memory database for these tests?
choices: Testcontainers makes each test method run in its own transaction that is rolled back automatically
The leaderboard is a native query that relies on PostgreSQL features such as RANK() over a window and LIMIT with a named parameter, which an in-memory database may handle differently or reject
An in-memory database cannot enforce unique constraints
Spring Boot cannot create a DataSource for H2 under @SpringBootTest

questions.prompt: MatchResultService.record calls saveAndFlush inside the try block. What would change if it called save instead?
choices: Nothing, because save always flushes immediately for entities with a generated id
The score validation would be skipped
The unique index would no longer apply to the row
Constraint violations could surface later, at flush or commit time, outside the try/catch, so callers might see a raw DataIntegrityViolationException rather than the domain exception

questions.prompt: The container field is static and annotated with @Container, and the test cleans data in @BeforeEach. What does this give the test class?
choices: One Postgres container shared by all test methods in the class, with rows removed before each test so tests do not depend on one another
A fresh container for every test method, so cleanup in @BeforeEach is redundant
A container shared across all test classes in the module, started once for the whole build
Automatic rollback of every test's data without any explicit cleanup
